# `install` command

Install previously built FoBiS artifacts, or clone, build, and install a GitHub-hosted Fortran project in one step.

```bash
fobis install [repo] [options]
```

How to use it, with examples: [Libraries and other build systems](/cookbook/libraries), [Dependencies](/cookbook/dependencies).

## All options

Arguments: `REPO`

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fobos`, `-f` | TEXT |  | Specify a "fobos" file named differently from "fobos" |
| `--fci` |  |  | Assume fobos inputs as case insensitive |
| `--mode` | TEXT |  | Select a mode defined into a fobos file |
| `--lmodes` |  |  | List the modes defined into a fobos file |
| `--build-dir`, `--dbld` | TEXT |  | Directory containing built objects [default: ./]; given here, it wins over the mode's build_dir |
| `--prefix`, `-p` | TEXT | `./` | Prefix path where built objects are installed [default: ./] |
| `--bin` | TEXT | `bin/` | Sub-directory for executables [default: bin/] |
| `--lib` | TEXT | `lib/` | Sub-directory for libraries [default: lib/] |
| `--include` | TEXT | `include/` | Sub-directory for include files [default: include/] |
| `--branch` | TEXT |  | Branch to check out when installing from GitHub |
| `--tag` | TEXT |  | Tag to check out when installing from GitHub |
| `--rev` | TEXT |  | Commit revision to check out when installing from GitHub |
| `--update` |  |  | Re-fetch (git pull) before building and installing |
| `--no-build` |  |  | Clone only — skip building and installing |
| `--deps-dir` | TEXT |  | Directory for cloning GitHub repositories [default: ~/.fobis/] |
| `--force-compile` |  |  | Force to (re-)compile all |
| `--colors` |  |  | Activate colors in shell prints |
| `--log`, `-l` |  |  | Activate log file creation |
| `--graph` |  |  | Generate a dependencies graph via graphviz |
| `--quiet`, `-q` |  |  | Less verbose output |
| `--verbose` |  |  | Extremely verbose output for debugging |
| `--jobs`, `-j` | INTEGER | `1` | Number of concurrent compilation jobs [default: 1] |
| `--makefile`, `-m` | TEXT |  | Generate a GNU Makefile for building the project |
